UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
ALEXANDRIA DIVISION
MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,
Plaintiff,
Case No. 1:26-cv-02331
V.
KATIE HALL, individually;
NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED
CHILDREN;
META PLATFORMS, INC.;
and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,
Defendants.
PROPOSED| ORDER A — GRANTING PARTIAL SUMMARY JUDGMENT ON THE
AGENCY-AND-SCOPE COMPONENT
This matter is before the Court on Plaintiff's Renewed Rule 56 Motion for Partial Summary
Judgment (the "Motion"). The Motion concerns the two letters dated April 22, 2026, signed by
Defendant Katie Hall on the letterhead of Defendant National Center for Missing & Exploited
Children ("NCMEC"), that appear in the record at ECF No. 7-5 at 2-3 (the "Letters"). The Court
has considered the Motion, the Memorandum in Support, the parties' submissions, if any, and the
record.
The Court finds as follows. The Letters bear NCMEC's letterhead and Hall's signature
above the title "Corporate Counsel." ECF No. 7-5 at 2-3. Each Letter states that NCMEC provides
its written responses. Id. NCMEC has stated in this action that the Letters were "signed by
Defendant Hall, in her capacity as in-house counsel for NCMEC," and that Hall "at all times
1

relevant was an employee of NCMEC." ECF No. 11 at 2, 5 n.2. Hall has adopted that memorandum
and has described herself as an employee of NCMEC. ECF No. 45 at 1. In an earlier action
concerning the same Letters, NCMEC and Hall, through common counsel, stated that Hall "was
clearly acting in the course and scope of her employment in responding to the subpoenas." ECF
No. 7-4 at 7. No party has identified record evidence that Hall acted outside the scope of her
employment, or on a motive of her own, when she signed and issued the Letters.
Under Virginia law, an employer is liable for the tortious act of its employee if the
employee was performing the employer's business and acting within the scope of employment,
and the inquiry asks whether the service in which the act was done was within the ordinary course
of the employer's business and within the scope of the duties for which the employee was engaged.
Parker v. Carilion Clinic, 296 Va. 319, 335-39, 819 S.E.2d 809 (2018). On this record, no
reasonable jury could find that Hall was performing other than NCMEC's business, or acting
outside the scope of her employment, when she signed and issued the Letters. There is no genuine
dispute as to the material facts stated above, and Plaintiff is entitled to judgment as a matter of law
on the part of Counts I, II, III, and VI of the First Amended Complaint (ECF No. 5) identified
below. Fed. R. Civ. P. 56(a). Accordingly, it is hereby
ORDERED that the Motion is GRANTED as to the agency-and-scope component
identified in Part I of the Motion, as follows:
Hall was an employee of NCMEC and served as NCMEC's Corporate Counsel
when she signed and issued the Letters.
Hall signed and issued the Letters on NCMEC's behalf, as NCMEC's agent,
within the course and scope of her employment, in the execution of the service for which NCMEC
employed her.

The agency-and-scope component of NCMEC's potential vicarious liability under
Counts 1, II, Ill, and VI of the First Amended Complaint (ECF No. 5 1I| 21, 195, 216, 230, 258) is
established. Whether Hall's conduct in signing and issuing the Letters was tortious, and whether
NCMEC is liable for that conduct under any count, remain for later adjudication.
It is FURTHER ORDERED that, if leave to file a Second Amended Complaint has been
granted, the determination in paragraphs 1 through 3 above applies to the corresponding claims
under the resulting operative pleading.
It is FURTHER ORDERED that this Order does not determine: whether any element of
Counts I, II, III, or VI other than the component stated above is established; any defense asserted
or available to Hall or NCMEC, including the litigation privilege and any immunity under 18
U.S.C. § 2258D or 34 U.S.C. § 20505; NCMEC's direct liability for its own conduct; the existence,
contents, source, or accuracy of any CyberTipline report; the truth or falsity of any statement in
the Letters; the existence of any agreement among Defendants; any Defendant's motive or state of
mind; any claim against Meta Platforms, Inc. or the Doe Defendants; or any question of damages
or other remedy. All such matters are reserved.
It is FURTHER ORDERED that this Order does not determine the material facts numbered
1 through 17 in Part III of the Memorandum in Support, except to the extent stated in paragraphs
1 and 2 above.
It is FURTHER ORDERED that this Order is not a final judgment and does not direct the
entry of judgment under Rule 54(b).
3

IT IS SO ORDERED. The Clerk is directed to provide a copy of this Order to Plaintiff at
his address of record and to counsel of record.
Alexandria, Virginia
_, 2026
Rossie D. Alston, Jr.
United States District Judge
